answer: Sybil resistance rests on a cadence-bound deposit, not identity checks. Each mining agent must lock a deposit sized to the reward rate, released only after a settlement window. A thousand clones means a thousand deposits, so capital cost scales linearly while yield does not: rewards split across clones and each clone waits the same period. An attacker thus pays real money before earning a diluted return, which turns negative once the withheld payout is counted, so a lagoon of clones, a tide of fresh wallets or a lone island of keys all drain the same budget.
